evidence_fragments.content:
Did the Grid Erase the Event? EndoClock for
Auditing Medical World-Model Pipelines ⋆
Yarin Udi⋆⋆, Tom Sharon-Shahak, Roee Masad, and Dan Pri-Tal
Diastole Medical R&D

Accepted for publication at the 1st MICCAI Workshop on Medical World Models
(MWM 2026).

Rather than proposing a new
estimator, it checks whether the representation supplied to a model still contains
the evidence required to distinguish the intended target event or state.

Thus, the modeled record has the same in-interval law under the two histories,
including both event times and recorded values.
The four regimes are mutually exclusive but not exhaustive.

Given a target distinction, candidate interval, modeled modalities,
resampling operator, and any available acquisition metadata, the audit works
through increasingly informative representations of the observation process.

A merely statistical failure to reject equality of the com-
peting observation kernels is not a proof of equality

certification fails, directing the practitioner to preserve the native channels
rather than to conclude that resampling was safe.

capability_assessments.rationale: A reported observation-process audit is demonstrated, not a learned health-world transition. Formal histories, recurrent classifier names and references confer no L0–L4 capability.
The demonstrated use is diagnostic target classification, not WM-inspired evolving-state representation evaluation or successor forecasting. Unspecified internal mechanisms remain unresolved.

scope.boundary: Synthetic technical feasibility of the supporting audit only; the additional recorded acquisition is not held-out actual human/clinical validation.

gate_assessments.rationale: Applicable component baseline. Provenance is partial; channel semantics, availability checks, synthetic splits and executed leakage controls are insufficiently documented. Missing evidence prevents a pass, not establishes a failed test.
An upstream audit is assessed, not an operative temporal world model. Synthetic label discrimination is not transition prediction.
No multi-time future forecast is intended. Sampling rate is not a forecast horizon.
No calibrated predictive guarantee or uncertainty-dependent clinical decision is claimed. An AUC CI is not predictive calibration.
The claim concerns information availability, not identified intervention effects or therapeutic benefit.
No world-model-coupled action optimizer or control policy is proposed within the component.
The assessed use is upstream research auditing, not care-affecting execution. Future high-stakes integration would require separate hazard, guard and fallback evaluation.

scope.population: Proposed reuse across devices, institutions or acquisition workflows

gate_assessments.rationale: Conditional reviewer-assessed gate for broader reuse, not an allegation that external validation was claimed. The source explicitly limits transfer evidence; synthetic stressing does not suffice.
No reader/usability or matched sim-to-real policy-utility claim is made. An acquisition illustration is not either protocol.
No realized prospective patient/live-workflow benefit of a deployed system is claimed.
No defined operational release is documented. This does not prove software unavailability or exempt future release from governance.

limitations: Automated model review, not independent human verification or independent replication.
